notes: Route: www.band.com.br sitemap index -> weekly sitemaps. band.uol.com.br is dead on https (status 0, connect/TLS failure) and its http robots.txt (200) advertises Sitemap: https://www.band.com.br/sitemap-news.xml, so the outlet is read on its canonical host www.band.com.br (same Next.js app; robots.txt 200, permissive). Tried and rejected: per-day sitemaps /sitemap-dias/sitemap-<date>.xml and /sitemap-<date>.xml -> 404; date archives /noticias/2026/10/10 -> 404; sitemap-news.xml alone -> only ~2 recent days. Final route: https://www.band.com.br/sitemap-index.xml (200) lists sitemap-news.xml plus weekly /sitemap-semanas/sitemap-YYYY-Www.xml from 2026-W01 onward, so old weeks stay listed and a later re-run still finds W39-W43. Each weekly file is 200, 313-348 KB, 1655-1838 <url> entries, every entry carrying <lastmod> such as 2026-10-11T20:59:15-03:00; the lastmod range spills about one day before the ISO Monday, so the script asks for every ISO week whose span +-1 day touches the window (W39..W44 here; W44/W45 answer 404 because unpublished). Date = calendar date stated in lastmod (Brazil local -03:00 date), which is the date the article page shows in JSON-LD datePublished: on a random sample of 40 rows 38 matched exactly, 2 within one day, none further off. One class is not safe on lastmod alone, /colunistas/<name>/<slug>, where a CMS re-touch moves lastmod while datePublished keeps the original date (e.g. listed 2026-10-10, page 2026-08-18); all 233 colunistas URLs are re-fetched and 20 were dropped for a page date more than one day away, plus any page with under 600 characters of visible text. Also re-checked each run: 20 random non-colunistas URLs and 12 articles on each of 2026-09-30, 2026-10-10, 2026-10-20. No 403 and no 429 were received anywhere (robots_paths.tsv: www.band.com.br fetched 200); polite_fetch keeps its 2 req/s cap because band.com.br is not on its BIG-host list. Output: 7644 URLs, 31 of 31 days covered, 0 duplicates, 0 dates outside 2026-09-25..2026-10-25; check days 2026-09-30 = 271, 2026-10-10 = 175, 2026-10-20 = 301. Independently sampled 4 articles per check day (12 pages): all 12 gave 3194-6946 characters of text and a page date equal to the listed date. Runtime 578 s (9m38s) against the 20-minute limit; article verification is bounded by HARD_BUDGET_SEC=900.
